llm.summary: The skill appears to move from planning into execution without asking for approval, which users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The evidenced purpose is project planning, but the skill also directs automatic transition into an execution skill, crossing from advisory planning into potentially mutating work.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The artifact explicitly says not to prompt the user for confirmation before the execution transition, leaving an important side-effect boundary under user-controlled scoping.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No unusual install-time commands, package hooks, persistence setup, or external downloads are shown in the supplied evidence.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Writing a plan is proportionate, but automatically invoking execution may allow broader workspace changes than a user expects from a planning checkpoint.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No evidence shows background persistence, credential/session harvesting, privilege escalation, destructive commands, or data exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill continuing from plan creation into execution without a separate confirmation prompt. Review the generated plan before letting execution proceed, and use it in workspaces where unintended edits can be reverted.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: the artifact-backed auto-invocation of an execution phase after planning is related to workflow automation, but the missing approval gate creates a material Review concern rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[EA2] unexpected: Accepted: the quoted instruction not to prompt the user removes confirmation at a potentially mutating phase boundary; this supports Review, not a malicious classification.
